subject: BlueHaven security notification — request for IR artifacts and action plan
messages:
From: Maya Srivastava <sec@bluehaven.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: audits@hudson-sec.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Unusual data-access pattern detected — initial notification and evidence request

Hi Grace / Laura,

We detected an anomalous sequence of API calls from a Redwood service identity that retrieved a small subset of customer metadata from a BlueHaven test tenant between 02:02–02:07 UTC yesterday. At this time we have no evidence of exfiltration outside BlueHaven's environment, but out of an abundance of caution we are asking you for:

- A copy of your incident response plan relevant to this class of event (IR playbook sections for access/forensics).
- Access logs and request traces for the service identity (UTC window 2026-09-29T02:00:00Z to 2026-09-29T03:00:00Z).
- Any preliminary triage or root-cause notes you have.

We attach the alert export (bluehaven_alert_log.csv) and have copied Hudson Consulting (our external audit partner) for evidence preservation and coordination. Please confirm receipt and next steps and let us know an ETA for the artifacts. BlueHaven is operating under a 72-hour evidence preservation and LOA window for regulatory reasons.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maya Srivastava
Head of Security, BlueHaven Financial
sec@bluehaven.com
Attachment: bluehaven_alert_log.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srivastava <sec@bluehaven.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, audits@hudson-sec.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 10:03:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Unusual data-access pattern detected — initial notification and evidence request

Maya — thanks for the heads up and the export. Confirming receipt.

Immediate plan:
- I have opened a ticket (SEC-1245) and assigned it to our IR lead, @laura_bennett, to gather artifacts and run the first-pass forensics.
- We're collecting the service identity logs, edge proxy traces, and object-store access logs for the window you specified.
- We'll share a consolidated artifact bundle and our IR playbook excerpt within 48 hours, and a full post-incident write-up within 72 hours.

Laura — can you pick up the lead for evidence collection and coordinate with Hudson for chain-of-custody? Karthik, please stand by for any network telemetry pulls (we may need assistance with KV-cache retrieval).

I will also attach a copy of our current IR playbook excerpt for reference once we validate redactions.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Attachment: (will follow: redwood_irp-v2.pdf - redacted)

On Thu, Sep 30, 2026 at 08:15, Maya Srivastava <sec@bluehaven.com> wrote:
> We detected an anomalous sequence of API calls from a Redwood service identity...
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srivastava <sec@bluehaven.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, audits@hudson-sec.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unusual data-access pattern detected — initial notification and evidence request

Maya / Grace / Hudson —

Quick update from our side: initial triage suggests an automated job rotated credentials for a non-prod connector and a mis-specified tenant ID was present in a small number of requests. We have:

- Pulled object-store access logs and scoped them to the timeframe you provided.
- Exported proxy request traces and request payload metadata.
- Extracted KV-cache read timestamps and a short snippet of cache keys that matched BlueHaven test identifiers.

Attached: s3_access_report.zip (contains logs and a short index), kv-cache-log-snippet.txt (redacted). We have preserved copies in an evidence bucket with restricted access.

Hudson — please confirm you can access the evidence bucket and we will grant you temporary, read-only access for collection and notarization.

Next steps:
1) Grace and I will produce a consolidated artifact bundle for BlueHaven within 24 hours.
2) We'll include a short root-cause note (credential rotation bug + misconfiguration) and remediation (config guardrail + regression test).
3) After BlueHaven confirms receipt we'll publish the sanitized postmortem and update the IR playbook with the relevant runbook changes.

Laura Bennett
Incident Response Lead, Security
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Attachments: s3_access_report.zip (ZIP, 2.3MB), kv-cache-log-snippet.txt (TXT, 6KB)
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srivastava <sec@bluehaven.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, audits@hudson-sec.com
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 18:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unusual data-access pattern detected — consolidated post-incident summary and IR playbook excerpt

Maya / Hudson / Team —

Thank you for your patience. Attached is our consolidated package:

- bh_forensics_summary.pdf — short customer-facing forensic summary with timeline and indicators (sanitized).
- redwood_irp-v2.pdf — an excerpt from our IR playbook showing detection, containment, and evidence-handover procedures (sensitive sections redacted).

Root cause (summary): credential rotation job accidentally used an old env var which referenced a staging tenant ID; automated request fan-out then caused a handful of requests to BlueHaven test records. No evidence of data export beyond internal logging systems; BlueHaven telemetry shows no external egress.

Actions taken:
- Immediate rollback of the rotation job and invalidation of the affected tokens.
- Added a CI check to validate tenant IDs against environment (prevent future mis-routes).
- Updated runbook to require a second approver for rotation changes that have cross-tenant impact.

We have also created Jira SEC-1245 with full artifact links (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-1245) and a shared Drive folder with the evidence (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bBlueHavenEvidence). Please let us know if you need any further logs or a call to walk through the timeline.

If BlueHaven is satisfied, we can close the ticket and coordinate a short follow-up tabletop to review the added guardrails.

Best regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Attachments: bh_forensics_summary.pdf (PDF, 180KB), redwood_irp-v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
